en.subtitle: Unix Shell Engine — automation blueprints, pipeline stream redirection, system permission management, and cross-platform automation via native Linux or Windows WSL frameworks.
en.s1_intro: Bash is the default execution interface for Linux environments. On Windows platforms, you can safely execute identical scripts utilizing **WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)** or Git Bash, bypassing native PowerShell formatting completely. Every script must explicitly declare its execution engine via a header construct called **Shebang**.
en.s2_intro: Interacting with the system requires traversing directory structures. Unlike Windows paths which utilize backslashes and drive letters (C:\), Unix environments map all elements down from a single root slash infrastructure.
en.s3_intro: Files must explicitly carry execution permissions to run as scripts. The operating system calculates security rights based on three user categories: **User (Owner), Group, and Others**.
en.s4_intro: Variables store dynamic configurations within a script context. **CRITICAL WARNING:** You must never leave trailing whitespaces around the assignment operator token (=); otherwise, the shell engine parses the target variable name as an executable system application command.
en.s5_intro: Branching flows rely on condition blocks evaluated via the [ ] syntax (which internally calls the system tool test). Strings use standard algebraic symbols, but numerical evaluations require specific flag operators.
en.s6_intro: Loops automate repetitive tasks, such as scanning text arrays or batch-modifying server log layouts, by processing structures over a structured collection block.
en.s7_intro: The true power of Bash lies in standard stream manipulation. By leveraging the pipe operator (|), you can redirect the text output of one script or command to serve as the direct input for the next processing block.
en.s8_intro: Every execution task runs in its own memory container track monitored via a unique **PID (Process ID)**. Bash lets you shift tasks to the background or terminate stalled processes instantly.

it.s8_title: Gestione Errori e Segnali con trap
it.s1_intro: In Bash le variabili sono stringhe prive di tipizzazione rigida. L'espansione dei parametri consente manipolazioni avanzate senza invocare comandi esterni.
it.s2_intro: I programmi Unix comunicano tramite tre flussi standard: stdin (0), stdout (1) e stderr (2), facilmente reindirizzabili su file o pipe.
it.s3_intro: L'operatore pipe (|) connette l'output di un processo all'input del successivo, consentendo pipeline di elaborazione dati potenti ed eleganti.
it.s4_intro: Bash offre il costrutto avanzato [[ ... ]] per valutare espressioni logiche, confrontare numeri e verificare l'esistenza di file.
it.s5_intro: I cicli consentono di iterare su elenchi di file, intervalli numerici e linee di testo provenienti da file o comandi.
it.s6_intro: Le funzioni consentono di incapsulare compiti riutilizzabili. È fondamentale dichiarare le variabili con local per prevenire conflitti globali.
it.s7_intro: La sintassi $(comando) esegue un'istruzione in una sottoshell catturandone direttamente l'output in una variabile.
it.s8_intro: Configurare set -euo pipefail e usare trap garantisce che lo script si arresti tempestivamente in caso di errore non gestito.

es.s1_intro: En Bash las variables almacenan texto sin tipos rígidos. La sintaxis de expansión permite recortar texto y asignar valores por defecto rápidamente.
es.s2_intro: Toda herramienta en Unix utiliza tres descriptores de archivo estándar: stdin (0), stdout (1) y stderr (2), permitiendo redirigir datos a disco.
es.s3_intro: El operador de tubería (|) transfiere la salida de un comando como entrada del siguiente, creando cadenas de procesamiento eficientes.
es.s4_intro: Bash incorpora el evaluador extendido [[ ... ]] para validar cadenas, probar existencia de archivos y realizar comparaciones numéricas seguras.
es.s5_intro: Los bucles facilitan iterar sobre colecciones de archivos, listas de valores o procesar líneas completas procedentes de archivos de texto.
es.s6_intro: Modularizar scripts en funciones mejora la claridad. Es crucial utilizar local para evitar sobreescribir variables en el entorno global.
es.s7_intro: La sintaxis $(comando) ejecuta procesos en una subshell aislada e inyecta su salida de texto directamente en variables o argumentos.
es.s8_intro: Incorporar set -euo pipefail e interceptar eventos con trap previene que los scripts continúen ejecutándose ante fallos inesperados.
